name: m88k-llvm-port
description: Reusable recipe that ports the out-of-tree m88k work to a new upstream LLVM release by rebasing the branch stack onto target_tag into a new branch release/NN.x-m88k (git rebase --onto, rerere), fixing API breakage in separate 'adapt to LLVM NN' commits, and diffing lit, compiler-rt and ncd19c bare-metal results against a baseline taken on the source stack. Parameters (inputs): repo_dir, upstream_dir, target_tag (required), source_ref, old_base, stack_order, release_branch, work_dir, build_dir, baseline_dir, baseline_build_dir, dry_run. Empty values are defaulted by step 'setup' (see PORTING.md). dry_run=true is read-only: preflight checks, conflict forecast with git merge-tree, and a lit-only baseline plus a self-diff to exercise the scripts; it never creates branches, worktrees or builds. STATUS: setup, preflight, baseline, replay are drafted and checkable with dry_run; build-fix loop, verify-run, triage, verify-review and report are DRAFTS that have not been run (first real use is the 22.1 port). Pauses for the user on: existing release branch, ambiguous conflict resolutions, a test regression that needs triage (upstream behavior change vs real m88k bug), stalled build-fix, expensive rebuilds. Reuse for the next release: change target_tag, set source_ref to the previous release branch, stack_order to that branch alone and old_base to the previous tag. Build limits: inputs build_jobs (default 6), load_limit (default 8), link_jobs (default 2); every ninja call is `ninja -j<build_jobs> -l<load_limit>`, run in the background with nohup. Resumable: steps are idempotent and check existing state (run dir files, release branch, worktree, replay-state.json) before redoing work.

steps.prompt:
Your cwd may not be the repo: use ABSOLUTE paths and `git -C` everywhere. Resolve the parameters of this m88k LLVM port run and prepare the run directory.

Raw inputs (an empty value means: use the default shown):
- repo_dir = "{{repo_dir}}" (default /home/mk2s/Documents/llvm-m88k)
- upstream_dir = "{{upstream_dir}}" (default /home/mk2s/Documents/llvm-project, a git checkout of upstream LLVM with all tags)
- target_tag = "{{target_tag}}" (REQUIRED, e.g. llvmorg-22.1.8; never default it, never hardcode a version)
- source_ref = "{{source_ref}}" (default: the tip of the previous port, i.e. the newest release/NN.x-m88k branch in repo_dir, else the tip of the current stack: clang-netbsd-kernel)
- old_base = "{{old_base}}" (the upstream commit/tag that the source stack was built on; default: `git merge-base source_ref upstream tag` of the newest upstream release tag it contains; for the first port this is 4590f755cf58)
- stack_order = "{{stack_order}}" (space separated branches, bottom to top; default "main-m88k gnu-asm-mode clang-netbsd-target clang-netbsd-kernel". For a later port from a single collapsed branch this is just that branch)
- release_branch = "{{release_branch}}" (default release/<NN>.x-m88k where NN is the major of target_tag; parse it from the tag, e.g. llvmorg-22.1.8 -> 22)
- work_dir = "{{work_dir}}" (default: sibling directory <repo_dir>-<NN>, a git worktree for the new branch, so the old stack and its build stay usable)
- build_dir = "{{build_dir}}" (default <work_dir>/build)
- baseline_dir = "{{baseline_dir}}" (default <repo_dir>/.agents/tasks/m88k-llvm-port/baseline-<source_ref with / replaced by ->)
- baseline_build_dir = "{{baseline_build_dir}}" (build dir of the SOURCE stack; default <repo_dir>/build)
- build_jobs = "{{build_jobs}}" (default 6; ninja -j value)
- load_limit = "{{load_limit}}" (default 8; ninja -l value)
- link_jobs = "{{link_jobs}}" (default 2; LLVM_PARALLEL_LINK_JOBS)
- dry_run = "{{dry_run}}" (default false; "true" means read-only checks only, see the recipe description)

Setup is idempotent and resumable: if a run directory for this target_tag already has run.json and a replay/build/triage state file, and the user is restarting after a killed session, reuse the newest such run dir (print its path) instead of creating a new one; otherwise create a new one. Do not start any build here.
Steps:
1. Read {{repo_dir}}/PORTING.md if present (if repo_dir is empty use /home/mk2s/Documents/llvm-m88k).
2. Verify target_tag exists in upstream_dir (`git -C upstream_dir rev-parse --verify refs/tags/<tag>^{commit}`) and that repo_dir has it too, or can fetch it from upstream_dir (`git -C repo_dir fetch <upstream_dir> tag <tag> --no-tags` is allowed; do not fetch from origin).
3. Create the run directory <repo_dir>/.agents/tasks/m88k-llvm-port/run-<target_tag>-<YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS>/ with a logs/ subdirectory.
4. Write <run dir>/run.json containing every resolved value (keys: repo_dir, upstream_dir, target_tag, llvm_major, source_ref, old_base, stack_order (array), release_branch, work_dir, build_dir, baseline_dir, baseline_build_dir, build_jobs, load_limit, link_jobs (integers), dry_run (boolean), run_dir, prior_adaptation_hints (short list distilled from PORTING.md sections of earlier releases)).
5. Gate files for dry runs: if dry_run is true, also write into <run dir> the files that gate the loops, each with a "dry_run": true flag: replay-state.json {"verdict":"DONE","dry_run":true}, build-review.json {"verdict":"APPROVED","dry_run":true}, triage-state.json {"verdict":"PASS","dry_run":true}, so the repeat loops exit at once and the dry run can complete. When dry_run is false write none of them.
In every later step, `<name>` in a prompt means the value of `name` in run.json (raw inputs may be empty; run.json is authoritative).
Your ENTIRE final response must be exactly the absolute run directory path and nothing else (no quotes, no prose); later steps consume it.

Your cwd may not be the repo: use ABSOLUTE paths and `git -C` everywhere. Resolved parameters for this run are in {{setup.output}}/run.json (use those, not the raw inputs, because empty inputs were defaulted there). Process notes and the per-release adaptation log are in <repo_dir>/PORTING.md: read it before you start. Never push, never use `git reset --hard`, `git clean`, or `branch -D`, never touch origin/* refs. MEMORY LIMITS (the 22.1 port was OOM-killed twice on a 14 GB machine): build_jobs, load_limit and link_jobs come from run.json. EVERY ninja call must be `ninja -j<build_jobs> -l<load_limit> ...` (never plain `ninja`, never `-j` of nproc). Run every build and other long command (ninja, lit, baseline script) in the background with nohup, logging into {{setup.output}}/logs/, and poll the log. Before starting any build, confirm no previous build process is alive (`pgrep -a ninja; pgrep -a "cc1|clang|ld.lld|ld"` restricted to this build dir) and that nothing else is running in the same build dir; if one is alive, wait or stop it deliberately, never start a second one. New build dirs are configured with -DLLVM_PARALLEL_LINK_JOBS=<link_jobs> -DLLVM_PARALLEL_COMPILE_JOBS=<build_jobs>. RESUMABLE: this recipe may be restarted after the session is killed. Every step must be idempotent: before doing work check existing state (run dir files such as run.json, replay-state.json, build-state.json, triage-state.json; whether release_branch and work_dir exist; the newest build log; whether baseline results.txt is complete) and continue from there instead of redoing or recreating it. If the release branch or worktree exists because of this run (replay-state.json present), reuse it without asking; ask only when it predates the run. Poll the log. MAME is always launched in window mode (run-ncd19c.py does this); it needs DISPLAY.

DRY RUN: if run.json has dry_run=true, do only the read-only checks named for this step, write their results, and do not modify any branch, worktree, build dir or PORTING.md. PHASE 1: preflight and backup. Write findings to {{setup.output}}/preflight.md.

Checks (all read-only):
a. Tools: git, cmake, ninja, python3, clang (host compiler), and for baremetal: DISPLAY set and <repo_dir>/../mame/mame or /home/mk2s/Documents/mame/mame present, <repo_dir>/m88k-baremetal/ncd19c/run-ncd19c.py present. Missing display or MAME is a warning for the baremetal phase, not a stop.
b. `git -C repo_dir config rerere.enabled` must be true; if not, report it. (When not dry_run you may run `git -C repo_dir config rerere.enabled true` and `rerere.autoupdate true`; this is the only config change allowed.)
c. Every branch in stack_order exists and each is an ancestor of the next (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`); the first one has old_base as an ancestor. Record commit counts per segment (`git rev-list --count prev..branch`) and the tip SHA of every branch and of source_ref.
d. repo_dir has no uncommitted TRACKED changes (untracked files are OK); the release_branch does not already exist (if it does, stop with send_message severity warning and ask whether to reuse or pick a new name); work_dir does not exist.
e. Disk space: at least 60 GB free on the filesystem of build_dir (`df`), RAM and nproc noted.
f. Scripts: bash -n on <repo_dir>/scripts/m88k-baseline.sh and m88k-baseline-diff.sh.
g. Conflict forecast (read-only, no worktree): for each stack segment run `git -C repo_dir merge-tree --write-tree --name-only --merge-base=<segment base> <target_tag> <segment tip>` and list conflicted paths. This is a whole-segment approximation of the real replay; write the lists to {{setup.output}}/conflict-forecast.txt.

Backup (SKIP when dry_run): for every branch in stack_order and source_ref create `refs/backup/<date>/<branch>` via `git update-ref`, and write a bundle `git -C repo_dir bundle create <repo_dir>/../m88k-backup-<date>.bundle <all those branches>` (verify with `git bundle verify`). Record bundle path and SHAs in {{setup.output}}/preflight.md.

Fail loudly: if a check marks the run unsafe, call send_message with severity warning and the reason, then stop.

Procedure (skip all of it on dry_run; the preflight forecast stands in):
1. `git -C repo_dir worktree add -b <release_branch> <work_dir> <target_tag>` (the new branch starts at the upstream tag; the tag must come from upstream_dir via fetch, never from origin).
2. cur = target_tag. For each branch B in stack_order, with prev = the previous branch tip SHA (for the first: old_base) taken from {{setup.output}}/preflight.md:
   - `git -C work_dir switch -C m88k-port/<B> <tip SHA of B>`
   - `git -C work_dir rebase --onto <cur> <prev>` (rerere is enabled so repeated identical conflicts resolve automatically)
   - on completion, cur = `git -C work_dir rev-parse HEAD`.
   If the rebase stops with conflicts, write the conflicted paths, upstream commit/area responsible (`git log -3 <target_tag> -- <path>`), and your resolution reasoning to conflicts.md, and stop this step: the replay loop below resolves them. Persist progress (segment index, cur, whether a rebase is in progress) in {{setup.output}}/replay-state.json with fields: verdict ("DONE" or "IN_PROGRESS"), segment, cur.
3. When all segments are done: `git -C work_dir switch <release_branch>` and `git -C work_dir merge --ff-only <cur>` (fast-forward only); verify `git -C work_dir rev-list --count <target_tag>..<release_branch>` equals the sum of the segment commit counts from preflight.md (squashed-away empty commits must be listed). Delete the temporary m88k-port/* branches only with `git branch -d` after the check. Set replay-state.json verdict DONE.

For each conflicted file, resolve it so the m88k intent is kept on top of upstream's new code (inspect `git diff --diff3`, `git log <target_tag> -3 -- <file>`, and the m88k commit being replayed). Do not take "ours/theirs" wholesale. Record each resolution in {{setup.output}}/conflicts.md (file, upstream cause, what you did). `git add`, `git rebase --continue`, and keep going through the remaining segments exactly as in step create-branch (same replay-state.json contract). A resolution that changes behavior visible to m88k users or that you are not sure preserves the m88k logic is a product decision: call send_message severity warning with the file, the options and your recommendation, and wait. If a conflict pattern is new, also note it for PORTING.md. When the last segment finishes and the branch is fast-forwarded, set verdict DONE in replay-state.json.

PHASE 4: bounded build-fix loop (DRAFT, untested). Make the m88k code build against {{target_tag}} one error cluster at a time. On dry_run do nothing.

State file {{setup.output}}/build-state.json: {"verdict":"PASS"|"FAIL","iteration":N,"errors_remaining":N,"last_commit":"sha"}. Write verdict PASS only when the full build below succeeded with no errors.

Each iteration:
1. First iteration only: if <build_dir>/build.ninja already exists skip configuring and reuse it; otherwise configure build_dir with -DLLVM_PARALLEL_LINK_JOBS=<link_jobs> -DLLVM_PARALLEL_COMPILE_JOBS=<build_jobs> and the same flags as baseline_build_dir (read <baseline_build_dir>/CMakeCache.txt: generator, CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE, LLVM_ENABLE_PROJECTS, LLVM_EXPERIMENTAL_TARGETS_TO_BUILD=M88k, LLVM_ENABLE_ASSERTIONS, host compiler) with `-S <work_dir>/llvm -B <build_dir>`. Add the projects the baseline lldb build used only when the baseline script's lldb step needs them (separate lldb build dir <build_dir>-lldb, same rule). Do not change flags just to make errors go away.
2. Build in the background: `nohup ninja -C <build_dir> -j<build_jobs> -l<load_limit> -k 0 clang lld llc llvm-mc llvm-objdump llvm-readobj llvm-nm llvm-ar llvm-ranlib llvm-config FileCheck count not llvm-lit > {{setup.output}}/logs/build-<iteration>.log 2>&1 &` and poll (first confirm no earlier ninja for this build_dir is still running). Use -k 0 so one pass shows all errors.
3. From the log pick ONE coherent cluster of errors in m88k code (llvm/lib/Target/M88k, clang/lib/*/M88k*, lld/ELF/Arch/M88k.cpp, lldb M88k plugin, m88k tests). Find the upstream cause: `git -C <upstream_dir> log -S'<symbol>' <old_base>..<target_tag> -- <path>` and read the commit message / docs/ReleaseNotes. Fix it minimally, in the style of upstream's own migration of other targets (look at how e.g. RISCV or Lanai changed in the same commit).
